subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If the 2nd, 3rd and 4th terms in the expansion of (a + x)ⁿ are respectively 240, 720 and 1080, then find the values of a, x and n.

mark_split.label: Find x and state all three

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.27 — LAQ chapter 3 Binomial Theorem, answer 20. Printed appearances: TS 16. recall_prompt: Say how you would find a, x and n — how you write the three terms, what dividing consecutive terms gives, how the two relations give n, and how you then get a and x.
insider_note: The 2nd term is Tᵣ₊₁ with r = 1, not r = 2. Divide consecutive terms so the powers of a and x cancel, and state all three values at the end — n alone is not the full answer.

steps.label: Write T₂, T₃, T₄
steps.margin_note: First mark. Tᵣ₊₁ = ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ xʳ. The 2nd term has r = 1, the 3rd has r = 2, the 4th has r = 3 — one less than the position every time.
steps.memory_tip: Tᵣ₊₁ = ⁿCᵣaⁿ⁻ʳxʳ, so the 2nd term has r = 1 — one less than the position, every time.
lines: In (a + x)ⁿ, Tᵣ₊₁ = ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ xʳ

recall.must_convey: That the 2nd, 3rd and 4th terms are ⁿC₁aⁿ⁻¹x, ⁿC₂aⁿ⁻²x², ⁿC₃aⁿ⁻³x³, set equal to 240, 720, 1080.
accept: write the second third and fourth terms using the general term and set them equal to two forty seven twenty and ten eighty
T two is n C one a to the n minus one x, T three is n C two a to the n minus two x squared and T four is n C three a to the n minus three x cubed
use T r plus one equals n C r a power n minus r x power r for r equal to one two and three
general term tho T two T three T four rasi two forty seven twenty ten eighty ki equal pettali
the three given terms are r equal to one two and three in the general term

steps.why: Three equations for three unknowns. Writing the general term once and substituting r = 1, 2, 3 is the only way to get all three equations without error.
common_mistakes: Taking the 2nd term as r = 2 — the r-th power of x appears in the (r + 1)-th term.
Writing xⁿ⁻ʳ aʳ: here a is the first entry of the bracket, so a carries n − r.

steps.label: Divide (2) by (1)
steps.margin_note: Second and third marks. Dividing removes the unknown power of a. ⁿC₂/ⁿC₁ = (n − 1)/2 comes from ⁿCᵣ₊₁/ⁿCᵣ = (n − r)/(r + 1) with r = 1.
steps.memory_tip: Dividing consecutive terms cancels the unknown power of a. ⁿC₂/ⁿC₁ = (n − 1)/2.

recall.must_convey: That dividing the 3rd term by the 2nd gives (n − 1)/2 times x/a = 3, so (n − 1)x = 6a.
accept: divide the third term by the second, the ratio of the C values is n minus one by two, times x by a equals three, so n minus one into x is six a
T three by T two is three which gives n minus one by two into x by a equals three
use n C r plus one over n C r equals n minus r over r plus one to get n minus one x equals six a
T three ni T two tho divide cheste n minus one into x equals six a vasthundi
the first ratio gives n minus one times x equals six a

steps.why: Ratios of consecutive terms remove the powers of a and leave n, x and a in one clean relation. Two such ratios are what solve the question.
common_mistakes: Dividing (1) by (2) and then treating 1/3 as 3.

steps.label: Divide (3) by (2)
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Same move one step up: ⁿC₃/ⁿC₂ = (n − 2)/3.
steps.memory_tip: The same move one step up: ⁿC₃/ⁿC₂ = (n − 2)/3, and 1080/720 = 3/2.

recall.must_convey: That dividing the 4th term by the 3rd gives (n − 2)/3 times x/a = 3/2, so 2(n − 2)x = 9a.
accept: divide the fourth term by the third to get n minus two by three into x by a equals three by two, so two into n minus two into x is nine a
T four by T three is three by two which gives two n minus two x equals nine a
the second ratio is ten eighty by seven twenty equals three by two
T four ni T three tho divide cheste two into n minus two into x equals nine a
n minus two by three times x by a equals three by two

steps.why: The second ratio is independent of the first, so together they pin n down. One ratio alone would leave x/a and n mixed together.

steps.label: Find n
steps.margin_note: Fifth mark. Divide (5) by (4): the x and the a cancel and only n is left.
steps.memory_tip: Divide (5) by (4): both x and a cancel, leaving n alone.

recall.must_convey: That dividing the two relations cancels x and a, giving 4(n − 2) = 3(n − 1) and n = 5.
accept: divide the two relations, x and a cancel, four n minus eight equals three n minus three, so n is five
two n minus two over n minus one equals three by two which gives n equal to five
n comes to five
rendu relations ni divide cheste x a cancel ayyi n five vasthundi
cross multiply four into n minus two equals three into n minus one and n is five

steps.why: Both relations contain the same product x·a-ratio, so dividing them is the fastest way to isolate n without ever knowing x or a.
common_mistakes: Cross-multiplying as 2(n − 2)·2 = 3(n − 1) and losing a factor.
Getting n = 5 but not checking it makes both (4) and (5) consistent.

steps.label: Find a
steps.margin_note: Sixth mark. With n = 5, (4) gives x = 3a/2. Put that and n = 5 into (1): 5·a⁴·(3a/2) = 240 gives a⁵ = 32.
steps.memory_tip: With n = 5, (4) gives x = 3a/2. Put it into (1): a⁵ = 32 = 2⁵.

recall.must_convey: That (4) with n = 5 gives x = 3a/2, and substituting into the first term gives a⁵ = 32 so a = 2.
accept: n is five so x is three a by two, put it in the first term, five a to the four into three a by two is two forty, a to the five is thirty two, a is two
substitute x equals three a by two into T two to get a to the fifth equals thirty two

five a to the fourth times three a by two equals two forty gives a equals two

steps.why: The ratios gave only the shape x = 3a/2; the actual size needs one of the original equations, and the first is the simplest.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the ⁵C₁ = 5 in the first term.

steps.label: Find x and state all three
steps.margin_note: Seventh mark. x = 3a/2 with a = 2 is x = 3. Check: T₂ = 5·2⁴·3 = 240.
steps.memory_tip: State all THREE values. Check T₂ = 5 · 2⁴ · 3 = 240.

recall.must_convey: That x = 3a/2 = 3, and the answer is a = 2, x = 3, n = 5.
accept: x is three a by two which is three, so a is two x is three and n is five

steps.why: All three unknowns were asked for. Substituting back into T₂ = 5·16·3 = 240 confirms the set in one line.
common_mistakes: Stating only n and a because x was found on the way and forgotten.
Not checking against 720 or 1080 when time allows.
